title: Palair Macedonian Airlines 301
summary: The Fokker 100 crashed shortly after takeoff in snowy conditions due to ice accumulation on the wings. The aircraft had been parked in snow and refueled; ice around the wing roots melted from fuel temperature but ice on the wingtips remained. The crew elected not to de-ice the aircraft and encountered control problems during takeoff that caused the crash.
probable_cause: Ice accumulation on the aircraft wings that was inadequately de-iced before takeoff. The crew conducted only a tactile check and opted not to use ground de-icing equipment.

factors.evidence: During the refueling, the ice around the wings' roots had melted due to the temperature of the fuel, while the ice on the tips hadn't.
The crew opted not to de-ice the aircraft, thinking that most of the ice had melted and the remaining was safe enough for flying.
A crew switch was conducted and a new set of pilots were brought in; the Macedonian co-pilot was undergoing training to transfer from Boeing 737 to Fokker 100.
The FSE performed a tactile check by rubbing his hand over the wings but did not request de-icing.
The aircraft eventually encountered control problems during takeoff, which caused it to crash.

events.text: The aircraft arrived in Skopje after a flight from Frankfurt, and was parked in Skopje in snowy conditions.
The aircraft was refueled with approximately 2,000 liters of fuel during which ice around the wings' roots had melted due to the temperature of the fuel.
A second refueling was commenced and the FSE performed a tactile check by rubbing his hand over the wings, but did not request de-icing.
The aircraft was cleared for take-off and eventually encountered control problems during takeoff, which caused it to crash.
